subject: Evostack private cluster intake — PV mapping & nodepool partition questions
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@evostack.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: alex.johnson@evostack.ai, procurement@evostack.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private cluster intake — PV binding and nodepool partitioning questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the product overview last week. We're starting the internal prep for an on-prem private deployment and I have a short list of technical questions to help scope the SOW and the preflight checklist. We're trying to finalize the storage & node architecture before the intake workshop.

Key questions:
- PVC binding model: do you recommend static PVs per tenant or dynamic provisioning with a bind-on-attach strategy for our multi-tenant workloads? Our workload mix: model serving (GPU), batch preprocessing (CPU), and short-lived inference workers.
- Storage classes: We expect a mix of local NVMe for KV caches, an encrypted blockstore for models, and an NFS-backed shared store for artifacts. Any guidance on CSIs you prefer or pitfalls you've seen in hybrid on-prem environments?
- Nodepool partitioning: we'd like a suggested minimum for separate nodepools (gpu, cpu-highmem, ephemeral) and whether Redwood recommends dedicated node pools per tenant vs shared pools with node selectors/tolerations.
- Encryption/KMS: we're using a customer-managed keyring (HashiCorp Vault + HSM). Any special integration notes or audit log expectations from Redwood Private?

Can you confirm whether your team needs sample PV naming conventions and an example CSI StorageClass YAML in advance of the workshop? If helpful, I can share our internal inventory (hostnames, racks) ahead of time.

Appreciate any quick pointers so our infra team can line up the right people.

Best,
Samir
Director of Cloud Ops | EvoStack

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private cluster intake — PV binding and nodepool partitioning questions

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

Quick guidance:
- PVC binding: recommended pattern is dynamic provisioning with bind-on-attach + topology-aware PVs for model blockstore (gives flexibility and predictable attachment behavior). We only suggest static pre-bound PVs for legacy appliances or when cryptographic attestation of the physical disk is required.
- StorageClass/CSI: prefer CSI driver set: csi-block (for encrypted blockstore), csi-local-nvme (for node-local KV caches), and nfs-client-provisioner for the shared artifacts tier. Avoid long-lived hostPath mounts. We'll share example YAMLs.
- Nodepools: suggest three base nodepools — gpu (taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule), cpu-highmem (high mem, no GPU), and ephemeral (fast-evict, local-ssd). Start with minimal sizes: gpu=3, cpu-highmem=5, ephemeral=4; we can right-size after telemetry. Per-tenant dedicated pools only if you need strict resource isolation or billing attribution. Shared pools + nodeSelectors + resource quotas usually suffice.
- KMS/audit: Redwood Private supports Vault integration via transit for DEKs and logs all key usage to the audit sink. We'll need an API endpoint and a service account with restricted ACLs.

Attachments: I've attached our intake checklist and a short PV mapping matrix (evostack-intake-checklist.xlsx, pv-matrix-v1.pdf) — they include sample StorageClass YAML and PV naming patterns.

Next steps:
1) Shared intake doc: please upload your inventory CSV (hostnames/racks) to the Drive link below.
2) Intake workshop: propose Wed 18 Nov 2026 10:00–11:30 PT. Attendees: Samir, Alex, EvoStack infra lead, Aditya, Neha (storage lead), Irene (networking).
3) Prework request: confirm whether any nodes are air-gapped or have asymmetric egress (we have a slightly different op model for air-gapped sites).

If that all sounds good I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: evostack-intake-checklist.xlsx, pv-matrix-v1.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private cluster intake — PV binding and nodepool partitioning questions

Looping in a couple of concise notes for the intake:

- Ephemeral vs block mapping: for model shards we should prefer encrypted blockstore with delayed binding to avoid hot-attach churn across racks. For KV caches, node-local NVMe with podAntiAffinity to prevent noisy neighbor hotspots.
- PVC reclaimPolicy: set to Retain for model block PVs to avoid accidental data loss during node decommission. We'll provide a small lifecycle script for reclaim + snapshot.
- CSI versions: recommend csi 5.x+ for block drivers — older versions create attach/detach flapping on some older kernels we've seen.
- Networking note (Irene): we'll need to coordinate MTU values and BGP peering windows ahead of the workshop; some EvoStack sites are on 9000 MTU while others are 1500.

I'll add these to the intake checklist and post the example StorageClass yamls to the drive link.

Thanks,
Neha
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
